rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: no criminal-history questions before a conditional offer
rules.requirement: A New Jersey landlord cannot ask about your criminal record, orally or on an application, until after making you a conditional offer, except about methamphetamine production on federally assisted premises or lifetime sex-offender registration. You may give the landlord evidence of errors in your record or of rehabilitation.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer

coverage.summary: All rental dwelling units statewide except units in owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Inquiries about methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex-offender registration are allowed.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties through the Division on Civil Rights: up to $1,000 for a first violation, up to $5,000 for a second within five years, and up to $10,000 for two or more prior violations within seven years. Also possible return of the application fee and up to $1,000 paid to the applicant. No private court action is allowed.
rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 46:8-55 (P.L. 2021, c.110, § 4; Fair Chance in Housing Act)
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: limits on criminal records considered after a conditional offer
rules.requirement: Even after a conditional offer, a New Jersey landlord may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records, or juvenile adjudications. It may consider only listed serious convictions, first-degree offenses within 6 years, second- or third-degree offenses within 4 years, and fourth-degree offenses within 1 year. If the landlord withdraws the offer, it must give written reasons and an individualized assessment, and you may request within 30 days, free of charge, all the information it relied on.
rules.key_value: Lookback: 1st degree 6 yrs; 2nd/3rd degree 4 yrs; 4th degree 1 yr

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: written disclosure before accepting an application fee
rules.requirement: Before taking any application fee, a New Jersey landlord must tell you in writing whether it reviews criminal history. It must also tell you that you may give evidence of errors in your record or of rehabilitation.
